financials_interim.notes: Company (standalone) operating_profit (1,169,598) derived the same way as Group: Gross Profit + Other Income - Admin - S&D (2,321,981+43,719-1,049,908-146,194); ties to PBT 913,177 after +Finance Income 197,389 -Finance Costs 453,810 (rounds to within Rs 1k). No NCI at Company level. short_term_borrowings includes current interest-bearing loans (7,766,504) + bank overdrafts (2,617,871). Company total_assets includes a large Investment in Subsidiaries balance (40,869,303) which rose materially from 12,345,795 a year earlier, reflecting the Group's FY2025/26 corporate restructuring/rights issue (Company stated capital rose from Rs 25,731k to Rs 4,748,108k per the equity statement) -- this is a standalone-entity structural item, not part of operating performance.

The filing's P&L does not present its own operating-profit subtotal -- operating_profit (1,931,837) is derived as Gross Profit + Other Income - Administrative Expenses - Selling & Distribution Expenses (4,849,665+72,344-2,681,176-308,997), and checked by adding Finance Income and deducting Finance Costs to confirm it ties exactly to the disclosed Profit Before Tax of 1,898,708 (1,931,837-499,260+466,132=1,898,709, off by 1 on rounding). Prior-year comparative operating_profit (2,035,917) derived and checked the same way (2,035,917-492,630+206,521=1,749,808 vs disclosed 1,749,807). No column-swap or dual-rendering ambiguity was found -- EPS ties cleanly to profit attributable to parent (1,284,617,898/1,137,533,596=1.13) and the balance sheet identity holds (total assets = total liabilities + equity, both periods). short_term_borrowings includes both 'Interest Bearing Loans and Borrowings' (current, 9,296,465) and 'Bank Overdrafts' (4,084,225) as both are genuine interest-bearing debt; total_liabilities/total_assets figures are as reported in the filing's own subtotals.

interim_updates.note_text: Asiri Hospital Holdings PLC (Group) grew revenue 9.1% YoY to Rs 9,516mn for the quarter ended 30 June 2026, with all four revenue lines up: Pre Care (OPD/channeling) Rs 3,993mn to Rs 4,379mn (+9.7%), Post Care (IPD) Rs 4,135mn to Rs 4,458mn (+7.8%), Pharmaceutical Rs 576mn to Rs 659mn (+14.5%), and Other services Rs 16mn to Rs 20mn. However, cost growth outpaced revenue: Administrative Expenses rose 19.4% (Rs 2,246mn to Rs 2,681mn) and Selling & Distribution Expenses rose 32.8% (Rs 233mn to Rs 309mn), so the derived operating profit subtotal actually fell 5.1% YoY (Rs 2,036mn to Rs 1,932mn) despite higher revenue and roughly flat gross margin (50.9% vs 50.9%). The headline Profit Before Tax nonetheless rose 8.5% (Rs 1,750mn to Rs 1,899mn) and PAT rose 11.1% (Rs 1,226mn to Rs 1,362mn), entirely because Finance Income more than doubled from Rs 207mn to Rs 466mn (+125.7%), a swing of about Rs 260mn that masks the underlying operating-cost pressure. The cash flow statement's Investing Activities section shows this Finance Income was linked to an active investment period: Rs 1,004mn was placed into new investment in shares and there was a Rs 353mn net change in interest in subsidiaries during the quarter. Group Finance Costs were roughly flat (Rs 492.6mn to Rs 499.3mn, +1.4%) despite Interest Bearing Loans and Borrowings (incl. overdrafts) rising, and Net Cash from Operating Activities fell from Rs 1,062mn to Rs 810mn as trade & other receivables and other current assets absorbed more working capital.
interim_updates.gaps_note: No QoQ comparison possible: no quarter closer to this one has been collected for ASIR -- this is the first financial_statements entry for this symbol. Balance sheet YoY (30 June 2025 vs 30 June 2026) figures are available in the filing and were checked for the equity/NCI roll-forward, but only P&L metrics are carried into the yoy_json here per this project's convention.
interim_updates.takeaway: PAT growth of +11.1% YoY is not driven by core hospital operations -- the derived operating profit (pre-finance-items) actually declined 5.1% as admin and selling costs outgrew revenue. The entire earnings beat comes from Finance Income more than doubling (Rs 207mn to Rs 466mn), tied to increased investment activity (new share investments of Rs 1,004mn, subsidiary interest changes of Rs 353mn) rather than hospital/pharmacy/lab throughput -- this is a finance-income-driven quarter, not a core-margin-expansion one.
operational_highlights: Group revenue Rs 9,516mn, +9.1% YoY, with growth across all four segments (Pre Care, Post Care, Pharmaceutical, Other)
Pre Care (OPD/channeling) revenue +9.7% to Rs 4,379mn; Post Care (IPD) +7.8% to Rs 4,458mn; Pharmaceutical +14.5% to Rs 659mn
Derived operating profit (before finance items) fell 5.1% YoY to Rs 1,932mn as Admin Expenses (+19.4%) and S&D Expenses (+32.8%) outgrew revenue
Finance Income more than doubled, Rs 207mn to Rs 466mn (+125.7%), the primary driver of the 8.5% PBT growth
Basic EPS Rs 1.13 vs Rs 1.02 prior year (+10.8%); no dividend declared in either period
Net Cash from Operating Activities fell from Rs 1,062mn to Rs 810mn on higher working-capital absorption
key_drivers: Finance Income (Group) -- rose from Rs 206.5mn to Rs 466.1mn (+125.7%), a ~Rs 260mn swing that is the sole reason PBT and PAT grew despite falling core operating profit; linked to Rs 1,004mn of new share investments and a Rs 353mn net change in interest in subsidiaries per the cash flow statement
Administrative Expenses -- Group +19.4% (Rs 2,246mn to Rs 2,681mn) and Selling & Distribution +32.8% (Rs 233mn to Rs 309mn), the main drag on core operating profitability
Pharmaceutical segment -- fastest-growing revenue line at +14.5% (Rs 576mn to Rs 659mn), though it remains the smallest of the three core segments
